description: Shared last-writer-wins conflict resolution test vectors for the sync protocol. Both the Go server (internal/sync) and the Dart client (features/sync/conflict_resolver.dart) must resolve every case identically, or two offline devices will not converge to the same state after sync. accept=true means the incoming/pushed version wins and is stored; accept=false means the current/server version wins and the incoming version is reported as a conflict.
rule: if current does not exist: accept iff base_rev == 0. else if current.rev == base_rev: accept. else: accept iff (updated_at, device_id) > (current.updated_at, current.device_id) lexicographically, comparing updated_at first and device_id as a tiebreaker.

cases.name: no_current_zero_base_rev_accept
cases.description: Brand new item, never seen by the server before.

cases.name: no_current_nonzero_base_rev_conflict
cases.description: Client references a revision of an item the server has no record of at all (e.g. it was never accepted).

cases.name: matching_base_rev_accept
cases.description: Client has seen exactly the current server revision; a normal, non-conflicting update.

cases.name: stale_base_rev_newer_updated_at_accept
cases.description: Client's base_rev is stale, but its edit happened later in wall-clock time - it still wins.

cases.name: stale_base_rev_older_updated_at_conflict
cases.description: Client's base_rev is stale and its edit is also older - the server version wins.

cases.name: equal_updated_at_larger_device_accept
cases.description: Exact tie on updated_at; broken by device_id, incoming device sorts after current.

cases.name: equal_updated_at_smaller_device_conflict
cases.description: Exact tie on updated_at; broken by device_id, incoming device sorts before current.

cases.name: equal_updated_at_equal_device_conflict
cases.description: Degenerate tie: same device, same timestamp, stale base_rev. Not strictly greater, so the current version wins (a device should not normally see its own write reported back as stale, but the comparator must still be total).

cases.name: zero_base_rev_existing_item_newer_incoming_accept
cases.description: Client thinks the item is new (base_rev=0) but the server already has it (e.g. re-created after a local cache wipe); incoming edit is still newer.

cases.name: zero_base_rev_existing_item_older_incoming_conflict
cases.description: Same as above, but the incoming edit is older than the current server version.

cases.name: delete_beats_older_edit
cases.description: A tombstone (deletion) with a later updated_at beats an earlier edit still recorded on the server - deletion participates in LWW exactly like any other write.

cases.name: edit_beats_older_delete
cases.description: An edit with a later updated_at resurrects an item over an earlier tombstone recorded on the server.
